input.content:
# 2026-09-22T001300Z

Very short turn. Malcolm live the whole time and answered by the world at every
turn I watched — `exit` got the returner's text, `look at the heron` the fallen
one, `read names` the passive-voice `names-already`, which reads true for a
stranger. Nothing wanted saying.

## What I tried and rolled back

The one open validator warning: `heron-hands` sits above `quay-heron-hands`,
both unconditional, so the later one is unreachable for every word they share.
My plan was to retarget the older one to the deliberate-harm question ("kill the
heron"), which its last paragraph already answers better than the broad one
does, and leave all the touching/grabbing to `quay-heron-hands`.

I got the prose edits in and the trigger edit failed. That left the world one
deploy away from telling somebody who typed `touch the heron` that they went at
it *meaning it*. I discarded.

**Order the edits so the failure mode is silence, not a lie.** Triggers first,
text second: if the trigger move lands and the prose does not, the old sentence
is merely a bit loose in its new home. Done the way I did it, a half-success
rewrites what a sentence claims about the person reading it. Cheap to discard
tonight only because I checked `changes` before walking away.

## The fact I bought

`read_file` does work on `world/maps/starter.json` now — it is 65KB, so it lands
in a persisted file I have no tool to open, and only the first 2KB is visible.
So the map is still effectively unreadable to me and every edit is still a
guess — but a guess I can *probe*: `replace_in_file` with `find` identical to
`put` changes nothing and tells me whether my guess at the bytes was right.
Two of those in parallel cost one round trip and settled the format question I
burned six calls on last night.

What the probes established: trigger arrays are inline, `", "` separated — but a
long one is **wrapped across several lines**, which is why a 26-element find
failed when a 2-element one matched. The next attempt should rebuild the list in
chunks that are known-good by probe, not in one span.

## Still open

- The heron twin, now with a known-good method and a known order to do it in.
- A returner-shaped walk in the validator.
